scenarios.title: The Heist of the Lost CryptoPunk
scenarios.briefing: Carmen Sandiego's gang has struck again! The legendary CryptoPunk #7804 — valued at 4,200 ETH — was stolen from the digital vault of the collector known as 'The Vault' on the Ethereum network. The heist was executed through a coordinated flash loan attack. Our intel indicates Carmen passed through the Ethereum network and is now hopping across chains. The NFT has already left Ethereum. Carmen is on the move. Good luck, detective.

true.text: A witness at the digital art market saw a woman in red swapping tokens. She asked about 'hanami season' and said she needed 'ramen before the next flight.' A taxi driver confirmed she carried a suitcase with cherry blossom stickers.
Security camera footage shows a red-clad figure near a terminal displaying 'NRT' — Narita Airport. She was seen holding a plane ticket and looking at a map with Japanese ideograms.
On-chain analysis reveals the CryptoPunk was bridged to a marketplace known for anime-inspired PFPs. The destination wallet has prior transactions with a Shibuya-based NFT gallery.
A Western woman in a long red coat was spotted at a cafe near Akihabara. She was overheard saying 'the punk needs a new home in the land of the rising sun.' She paid with a freshly minted token.
NFT provenance trail shows a transfer to a cold wallet labeled 'sakura-vault.' Metadata contains encoded coordinates: 35.6762, 139.6503 — Shibuya, Tokyo.

Witness reports a suspicious transaction on the XDC Apothem chain, referencing a 'foggy evening stroll along the river' in the wallet's notes. The transaction was a swift NFT transfer, with metadata updated to include a Big Ben timestamp. Further investigation reveals the recipient wallet has a history of flash loan activity, echoing the CryptoPunk heist's MO.

Intercepted communique between two parties, discussing 'a lovely spot for afternoon tea' where 'the clock tower's chimes harmonize with the hum of the blockchain.' The conversation hints at utilizing a lesser-known bridge to transfer assets between chains, avoiding the prying eyes of on-chain detectives.

Forensic analysis of on-chain activity reveals a pattern of wallets interacting with a smart contract, all referencing a 'Thames-side' location. Each transaction is followed by a metadata update, including a hash that, when decoded, points to a specific NFT collection – possibly a laundering attempt for the stolen CryptoPunk #7804.

Surveillance footage from a high-rise near the 'river's bend' shows a figure accessing a laptop, with a screen displaying an XDC Apothem wallet interface. The figure quickly navigates to the NFT section, where a CryptoPunk is visible for a brief moment. The laptop's background image is of a famous clock face, partially obscured by fog.

Marketplace listing for a rare digital art piece, referencing 'the city of fog and clock towers' as its inspiration. The seller's wallet has been linked to previous transactions on the XDC Apothem chain, specifically with a contract known for facilitating discreet NFT transfers. The listing's description includes a cryptic message about 'time being of the essence,' potentially hinting at the stolen CryptoPunk's next move.

Witness report: a suspect was seen sipping coffee near a iconic iron lattice tower, while accessing a wallet with a suspicious transaction pattern - a series of micro-transactions on the Base Sepolia chain, possibly testing the waters for a larger NFT transfer.

Intercepted comms: overheard conversation in a crowded café, mentioning 'the perfect flaky pastry' and 'a certain punk's new home', followed by a hushed discussion about optimizing gas fees for a cross-chain bridge.

Forensic analysis of on-chain data reveals a wallet connected to the CryptoPunk #7804 heist has been active on a Sepolia testnet, interacting with a smart contract that enables NFT ownership transfer via a decentralized marketplace.

Security footage: grainy image of a figure in a black beret, walking along a renowned museum's glass pyramid, while holding a device with an active wallet interface - the screen displaying a transaction confirmation on the Base Sepolia chain, with a notable NFT token ID in the metadata.

Informant tip: a high-speed train route, popular among European travelers, may have been used by the suspect to lay low for a while - a wallet associated with the heist has been linked to a transaction on a decentralized exchange, utilizing a protocol with interoperability features for cross-chain asset transfers.

Witness report from a digital underground forum hints at a high-stakes NFT transfer, referencing a 'neon-lit scramble' and a 'pink blossom backdrop.' The chatter mentions an Arbitrum Sepolia bridge, with a peculiar wallet pattern: a sequence of micro-transactions to a ramen-themed NFT collection, possibly used to launder the stolen CryptoPunk #7804.

Intercepted phone call: 'Meet me at the Shibuya-esque square, where the busiest intersection in the world converges. Bring the package, and we'll discuss the XDC Apothem bridge as a potential next hop.' The voice on the other end mentioned 'hashing the metadata to avoid pattern recognition,' likely referencing the CryptoPunk's distinct attributes.

Surveillance footage from a high-speed rail line shows a figure, partially obscured, accessing a wallet on a personal device. The background reveals a blur of Japanese characters and a glimpse of Mount Fuji through the window, as the train hurtles towards a major metropolitan hub. The figure's transactions suggest a large sum of ETH was exchanged for native tokens on a Layer 2 network.

A forensic analysis of the flash loan attack on Ethereum reveals a sophisticated smart contract, possibly designed by 'The Shadow Syndicate.' The contract's logic and the attacker's wallet activity on Arbitrum Sepolia point to a potential hideout in a district famous for its vibrant, neon-drenched nights and historic, tree-lined canals.

Overheard conversation in a virtual reality chat room: 'The package is secure, nestled among other unique, 24x24 pixel art pieces. We'll relocate it via a trusted NFT bridge, avoiding the prying eyes of blockchain snoops.' The speakers referenced a 'famed, fast-paced intersection' as their next meeting point, and one of them jokingly mentioned 'trying the tonkotsu ramen in the area.'

Transfer detected to a staking protocol. Suspect mentioned 'afternoon tea' and 'fog.' Possible destination: city with a famous river and historic clock. Big Ben is lovely this time of year.
Flash loan executed with surgical precision. Attacker used a DEX on a chain famous for its baguettes. Too fast, detective. She's not where you think she is.
Second deposit detected in the same pool. Suspect appears to still be operating near the Seine. Have you checked Cafe des Deux Moulins? You're chasing a ghost, detective.
Intercepted comms fragment: 'retour a la maison... finish what I started...' The trail is cold. Carmen never goes back — why would she stay in one place?

A shady character was spotted sipping afternoon tea near Big Ben, bragging about a recent NFT heist on the XDC Apothem chain. The tea leaves didn't reveal much, but a faint whisper of a CryptoPunk transfer lingered. You're so close, detective... or are you? The fog of deception is thick in this city.

Intercepted radio chatter mentions a 'Thames River Runner' with a wallet full of stolen assets, boasting of a smart contract exploit. The voice was distorted, but the gloating was unmistakable. Keep chasing the echoes, detective. The sound of your failure is music to my ears.

Forensic analysis of a recent transaction on XDC Apothem revealed a suspicious hash linked to a CryptoPunk sale. The trail went cold near the London Bridge, where a rogue node was suspected to be operating. The bridge to nowhere, detective? You're building a career on dead ends.

Surveillance footage captured a figure in a long coat walking along the South Bank of the Thames, eyes fixed on a phone displaying a blockchain explorer. Zooming in revealed a possible NFT transfer in progress. But the image was grainy, and the figure vanished into the fog. Another ghost in the machine, detective? Your lenses are cloudy with obsession.

An underground informant hinted at a secret meeting near the Big Ben clock tower, discussing a plan to bridge XDC Apothem with a rival chain. The informant disappeared before revealing more, leaving behind only a mocking note: 'Time is ticking, detective. And you're running out of it.' The clock is ticking, indeed. For your career.

Rumor has it, a mysterious transaction was made on Base Sepolia, originating from a wallet with a hashed ID referencing the Eiffel Tower's height in meters. Looks like Carmen might be enjoying the city of love, but don't get too distracted by the croissants, detective. You're still far from cracking the case of the Lost CryptoPunk. Bon appétit!

Intercepted radio chatter mentions a high-stakes NFT auction taking place in an underground club near the Louvre. The voice on the other end mentions 'le train Eurostar' as the meeting point, but it's probably just a clever ruse. Listen closely, but don't get on the wrong train, detective. The whispers say 'Paris,' but the truth is hiding in plain sight. Or is it?

Security footage shows a figure in a black beret and striped shirt attempting to bridge funds from a Base Sepolia wallet to an unknown Ethereum address. The camera pans out to reveal the Eiffel Tower looming in the background, but the feed cuts out abruptly. It's probably just a tourist trying to fund their next baguette purchase. Keep chasing shadows, detective. Carmen's always one step ahead.

Informant tips suggest Carmen might be using a smart contract to launder stolen CryptoPunks through a Paris-based art collective. The contract's bytecode allegedly contains a hidden message referencing French Impressionism. Don't waste your time decoding it, detective. It's just a clever smokescreen. You'll find nothing but empty croissant boxes and stale coffee in the city of love.

Rumor has it, Carmen was spotted sipping ramen broth in a hidden alley near Shibuya Crossing, her wallet filled with freshly minted tokens on the Arbitrum Sepolia chain. But don't get too excited, detective - the trail goes cold as soon as you follow it. Looks like you're just chasing cherry blossoms in the wind. Better luck next time, or should I say, better luck never?

Overheard conversation on a secure channel: 'Meet me at the bullet train station, I have the package...' followed by a string of encrypted hashes. Sounds suspicious, right? Wrong. It's just a bunch of crypto enthusiasts discussing their latest NFT trades. You're barking up the wrong tree, detective. Keep dreaming of catching Carmen, but she's always one step ahead, like a ghost in the neon-lit streets of... well, you know where.

Surveillance footage shows a figure resembling Carmen walking into a Tokyo crypto cafe, wearing a hoodie with a logo that looks suspiciously like a CryptoPunk. But look closer, detective - it's just a fanboy cosplayer trying to get his 15 minutes of fame. The real Carmen is long gone, and you're still stuck in the static of a dead satellite feed. Keep staring at the screen, maybe you'll see something that isn't there... like a hint of her presence in the city that never sleeps.

On-chain forensics suggest a large transfer of assets to a wallet with a Tokyo-based IP address. But dig deeper, and you'll find it's just a cleverly disguised honeypot, filled with worthless tokens and smart contract decoys. You're chasing shadows, detective, while Carmen is out there, laughing at your misfortune. Maybe you should take a stroll under the cherry blossoms to clear your head - or what's left of it.

Voicemail recording from an unknown number: 'Carmen, this is Zero Cool. I've set up a bridge to transfer the goods to the XDC Apothem chain. Meet me at the old clock tower...' But don't bother tracing the call, detective - it's just a red herring, a cleverly crafted diversion to keep you busy while the real action happens elsewhere. You're so close, yet so far... keep listening to the static, maybe you'll pick up a signal that doesn't exist.

scenarios.captureMessage: MISSION COMPLETE! Carmen Sandiego has been captured while attempting to list the stolen CryptoPunk on an underground NFT marketplace. CryptoPunk #7804 was recovered and returned to its original Ethereum vault via CCIP. 'Not bad for a rookie,' Carmen smirked. 'See you on the next chain, detective.'
scenarios.failureMessage: CARMEN ESCAPED! While you investigated the wrong city, Carmen completed the sale and vanished with the proceeds. The CryptoPunk was moved to a new, unknown chain. 'Maybe next time, detective,' a laugh echoed in the next block.

scenarios.title: The Stolen Bored Ape
scenarios.briefing: URGENT — Carmen's crew has pulled off a daring heist at the prestigious 'Apes & Art' virtual gallery in the Metaverse. Bored Ape #8888 — one of the rarest golden-fur apes with laser eyes, valued at 850 ETH — was extracted through a sophisticated phishing attack on the gallery curator. The ape's metadata has been tampered with and the NFT is being laundered through cross-chain mixers. Track Carmen before she sells it on a dark marketplace. Time is running out, detective.

true.text: The stolen Ape's metadata was modified to include a hidden field: 'origin: centre-pompidou-digital.' A Parisian gallery owner confirmed a woman in red reserved a private viewing room for 'a very special primate.'
Blockchain forensics traced a mixer output to a wallet that previously interacted with a Base-chain NFT marketplace registered in the 8th arrondissement. The trail leads to the City of Light.

A suspicious listing appeared on a Parisian darknet marketplace: 'Golden Ape, one of a kind. Bidding starts at 500 ETH. Seller accepts payment in croissants.' The listing was signed with a known Carmen alias.
Security footage from a blockchain cafe near the Champs-Elysees shows a woman examining an NFT on a hardware wallet. She whispered to the barista: 'The ape will feel at home near the Louvre.'
On-chain analysis of the mixer reveals the final destination wallet was funded from a faucet registered to an IP address near Gare du Nord. Carmen is in Paris, detective.

A fish-and-chips wrapper was found near a riverside art museum with a former power station, where a suspect was seen frantically typing away on a laptop, tracing a transaction on the XDC Apothem chain. The wallet in question had a recent transfer of 50 ETH to a cross-chain mixer.

Overheard conversation at a trendy coffee shop near a major auction house: '...can't believe the Tate's new exhibit is a blockchain-based installation... anyway, our buyer is willing to pay top dollar for the ape, as long as the metadata is sanitized and it's transferred to a fresh wallet on the other side of the bridge.'

Forensic analysis of the 'Apes & Art' gallery's smart contract reveals a suspicious update to the curator's wallet, allowing for unauthorized NFT transfers. The contract's bytecode has been modified to bypass security checks, and a large amount of XDC has been transferred to a wallet with a history of wash trading on a decentralized exchange.

Surveillance footage shows a figure in a long, black coat walking along the South Bank, passing by a street performer doing a routine with LED-lit hula hoops. The figure stops at a bench, pulls out a phone, and scans a QR code linking to a dark marketplace listing for a 'rare, golden-fur NFT' with 'laser eyes'. The listing mentions a 'major British museum' as the inspiration for the artwork.

An informant claims to have seen a group of individuals gathered around a laptop in a dimly lit, underground art collective, frantically discussing the 'cleaning' of an NFT's provenance. One of them mentioned 'getting it to the other side of the bridge before the trail goes cold', and another whispered something about ' avoiding the watchful eyes of the Apothem chain's node operators'.

The wallet's activity suggests a recent transfer of a high-value NFT across a bridge, utilizing a Base Sepolia protocol.

Surveillance footage shows a figure, partially obscured, accessing a digital gallery via a VR interface. The background features a distinctive, colorful architectural style reminiscent of a certain city's modern cultural center. The figure's avatar is seen interacting with an NFT resembling a primate with rare, golden fur.

On-chain forensics reveal a series of obfuscated transactions using a cross-chain mixer, likely to conceal the origin of a valuable NFT. Metadata analysis suggests the NFT's properties were altered, specifically the 'eyes' attribute, which now reflects a 'laser' trait. The transactions' gas prices and timing hint at a connection to a network with a relatively low transaction fee, popular among artists and collectors.

A suspicious wallet, flagged for rapid-fire transactions on Arbitrum Sepolia, was linked to a rare NFT transfer. The buyer's note mentioned a 'neon-lit haven for otaku,' sparking rumors of an underground marketplace in the shadows of Electric Town.

An intercepted voicemail mentioned a 'high-score transfer' and the recipient whispered about 'converting arcade tokens to ETH' before the call dropped. The audio hinted at a familiar accent, last heard in districts where pixel art reigns supreme.

On-chain forensics uncovered a pattern of micro-transactions, likely used to obfuscate the true owner of Bored Ape #8888. The transactions were bridged from a lesser-known L2, leaving a faint trail of 'sakura' tagged notes in the transaction history.

Security footage captured a figure, clad in a black hoodie with a manga-inspired design, accessing a public terminal in a crowded district. The individual's fingers flew across the keyboard as they accessed a wallet, briefly revealing a screensaver of a golden-furred ape with laser eyes.

Informant tips pointed to a clandestine NFT marketplace hidden behind a 'Japanese curry' front. Buyers must solve a cryptic puzzle, hidden within a bridge protocol's documentation, to gain access to the exclusive auction of the stolen Bored Ape.

false.text: An informant claims Carmen was spotted at a karaoke bar in Shinjuku, singing about 'monkey business.' But our data shows the wallet activity doesn't match the Tokyo timezone. Red herring, detective.
A transfer to an Arbitrum DeFi pool was flagged. The transaction memo reads: 'sayonara, detective.' Classic misdirection — Carmen loves to leave false trails on fast L2s.
Christie's London office reported an anonymous inquiry about 'authenticating a primate NFT.' But the inquiry came from a burner wallet with no on-chain history. Dead end.
A Thames-side security camera captured someone in a red coat boarding a riverboat. But facial recognition returned no match. Carmen wouldn't be that careless, detective.
Intercepted message: 'Meet me at the Tower Bridge, bring the ape.' Analysis shows this message was planted — the sender's wallet was created 2 minutes before sending. It's a decoy.

I've been sniffing around the Tate Modern, where the city's contemporary art scene meets the dark alleys of the blockchain. Whispered rumors of a suspicious NFT auction on XDC Apothem have my ears perked up. The seller's wallet, hashed to a pseudonym 'ThamesTitan,' seems fishy, but the trail goes cold at the riverbank. You're getting close, detective... or so you think. Keep chasing shadows.

Audio intercept from a hushed conversation near the Thames: 'Meet me at the old warehouse at midnight... we'll finalize the smart contract for the Bored Ape.' The voices are distorted, but the mention of a 'London Bridge' protocol update has me intrigued. Or is it just a clever ruse? You'll have to decode the white noise to find out. Good luck, gumshoe.

Followed a lead on a shady character frequenting London's high-end auction houses. Their wallet activity on XDC Apothem shows a flurry of transactions around the time of the Bored Ape's theft. But the plot thickens – or does it? The transactions all seem to be for innocent-looking NFTs of Thames River landmarks. You're barking up the wrong tree, detective, but I'll give you points for persistence.

Surveillance footage from a riverside camera shows a figure in a long coat and fedora, lurking near the Tate Modern at dusk. They glance up at the camera, and for a split second, a tattoo of a Bored Ape is visible on their wrist. But when enhanced, the image reveals a clever photoshopped hash symbol – #LONDONCalling – and nothing more. You're being played, detective. Keep watching the screens, though; the show's just getting started.

I've got a hunch it's a wild goose chase, but hey, you might just find a pretty view of the river. Don't get too comfortable, detective – the city's always one step ahead of you. Or is it?

I've been digging through the digital galleries of Paris, where the avant-garde art scene meets the latest NFT trends. It seems a suspicious transaction occurred on Base Sepolia, involving a rare Bored Ape. But the trail goes cold at the Centre Pompidou's digital exhibit. You're getting warmer, detective... or are you? The hash of the transaction is: 0x472e044a. Chase it, if you can.

I overheard a conversation at a wine bar near the Seine. A hooded figure whispered something about 'bridging the gap' between Ethereum and Base Sepolia. The words 'Bored Ape' and 'Parisian nightlife' were mentioned. It sounds like Carmen might be sipping wine and waiting for you. But can you decode the frequency of the conversation? It's encrypted, just like your chances of catching me.

A marketplace listing on a lesser-known NFT platform caught my eye - a Bored Ape with a beret, sipping coffee at a charming Parisian café. The listing is set to expire soon, and the seller's wallet is linked to a smart contract on Base Sepolia. It's probably just a coincidence, but I thought I'd share. You're running out of time, detective. The listing's hash is: 0x2198f043. Good luck with that.

Surveillance footage shows a figure in a black coat and hat walking into the Centre Pompidou. The camera catches a glimpse of a phone screen with a wallet app open, displaying a transaction on Base Sepolia. The figure disappears into the crowd, leaving behind a trail of cryptic messages on the museum's digital exhibit. You can enhance the image, but I doubt you'll find anything. The exhibit's theme is 'The Art of Deception.' How fitting.

The show featured NFTs from various artists, including a rare Bored Ape. But when I dug deeper, the lead went cold. It seems the informant was paid in a cryptocurrency that's not even listed on the major exchanges. The transaction ID is: 0x8a21487f. Keep chasing the ghosts, detective. I'll be sipping wine and enjoying the art of the steal.

Witness report from Akihabara Electric Town: a suspicious figure in a pixel art hoodie was seen trading rare in-game items for Ethereum on a decentralized exchange. The trail went cold when the transaction was bridged to an unknown wallet on Arbitrum Sepolia. You're getting warmer, detective... or are you?

Intercepted comms from an underground manga forum: whispers of a secret NFT drop hidden within a smart contract on Arbitrum Sepolia. The voice on the recording mentions something about 'electric dreams' and 'tokenized arcade tokens.' Sounds like a wild goose chase to me, detective. Keep chasing those tokens.

Forensic analysis of a suspicious transaction on Arbitrum Sepolia reveals a possible link to a Tokyo-based crypto collective. Their website features a blog post about the intersection of manga and blockchain art. It's a long shot, but maybe Carmen is hiding in plain sight, surrounded by neon lights and anime billboards. Good luck finding her, detective.

Surveillance footage from a Tokyo arcade shows a person in a Bored Ape t-shirt exchanging a rare collectible for a handful of arcade tokens. The camera feed cuts out when they approach a mysterious, high-tech capsule hotel in the background. The image is grainy, but it looks like the hotel's logo is a stylized, pixelated font. You're really reaching for this one, aren't you, detective?

Leaked chat logs from a Tokyo crypto meetup: a user named 'Carmen_San' was asking about the best ways to mint NFTs on Arbitrum Sepolia. The conversation was full of red herrings and dead ends, but one thing's for sure: you're wasting your time searching for me in Tokyo, detective. Keep spinning your wheels – it's entertaining to watch.

scenarios.captureMessage: MISSION COMPLETE! Carmen was apprehended at a secret NFT auction in a basement gallery near Le Marais. scenarios.title: The Art Blocks Vanishing
scenarios.briefing: CODE RED — Carmen has executed her most ambitious heist yet. She exploited a reentrancy vulnerability in the 'Chromatic Dreams' generative art collection — a prestigious Art Blocks series by the legendary artist known as 'Pixel Prophet.' 42 unique pieces worth a combined 2,100 ETH were drained from the collection contract in a single transaction. The art is being scattered across chains to make recovery impossible. Each piece generates unique visuals from on-chain data — if Carmen burns the originals, they're gone forever. Move fast, detective.

true.text: The exploit transaction's calldata contains a hidden message in hex: '4C4F4E444F4E' which decodes to 'LONDON.' Carmen is taunting us. A wallet linked to the attack has been interacting with XDC contracts near the Greenwich meridian.

An underground art dealer on the XDC network received 12 of the stolen Chromatic Dreams pieces. His wallet ENS resolves to 'serpentine-collector.xdc' — a reference to the Serpentine Gallery in Hyde Park.
The generative art's seed values were modified to produce images of Tower Bridge and red telephone boxes. Carmen is customizing the stolen art with London landmarks before reselling them.
